problem: Existing VLN agents lack robust indoor scene (room-type) recognition, which limits their spatial perception and environmental understanding; there is also no dedicated dataset for it, and room categories are heavily imbalanced in MP3D data.
motivation: Recognizing the room type an agent is in is a key ingredient for grounding instructions such as 'go to the kitchen' and for spatial understanding in VLN. Room categories in Matterport3D are imbalanced, so classifiers perform poorly on rare classes, which motivates data augmentation via generative models.
key_idea: Build the R2R-SR room-classification dataset from MP3D and rebalance it by generating panoramic environment images with LLaVA (captioning) and Stable Diffusion (synthesis) as data augmentation (LSDA).
insight: Only the abstract was available, so ablations cannot be cited. The abstract claims that generative augmentation for under-represented room classes improves recognition over CNN and ViT baselines, which suggests data imbalance is a main bottleneck for scene recognition in VLN.
method: R2R-SR dataset: 7,283 images from the Matterport3D simulator labeled into 10 room classes, for indoor scene recognition in VLN.
LSDA augmentation: uses LLaVA to describe scenes and Stable Diffusion to generate panoramic environment images for under-represented room categories, to rebalance the training data.
LSDA-based recognition model: a classifier trained on the real plus generated data, reaching 75.9% Top-1 accuracy and outperforming the best CNN and ViT baselines.

setting.backbone: Image classifier (CNN/ViT-type) trained with LLaVA + Stable Diffusion augmented data; exact architecture not given in the abstract
setting.training_data: R2R-SR (7,283 MP3D images, 10 room classes) plus synthetic panoramas generated with LLaVA and Stable Diffusion
setting.observation: RGB images/panoramas from the Matterport3D simulator

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract reports Top-1 accuracy of 75.9% on R2R-SR, which is not a navigation benchmark so it is not listed.
results: The LSDA-based model achieves 75.9% Top-1 accuracy on the R2R-SR room classification task, outperforming the best CNN and ViT competitors. Qualitative results show it can identify distinctive features across room categories.
limitations: Evaluated only on scene classification; the abstract shows no demonstrated improvement in VLN navigation performance.
Synthetic images may have a domain gap from real MP3D views, and the dataset is small with only 10 classes.
